article_title: Podman 6.1 Adds Volume Rename, Machine Restart, and a Quadlet ImageVolume Key
summary: Well-sourced and technically accurate, but one quoted phrase is misattributed to the release notes when it actually comes from the secondary source's paraphrase.

findings.message: The article quotes the release notes as saying volume rename lets users rename volumes "without recreating them," but this exact phrase does not appear anywhere in GitHub's v6.1.0 release notes. It appears in Linuxiac's article instead ("allows users to rename existing Podman volumes without recreating them"). The release notes themselves say only: "A new command has been added, podman volume rename, to allow renaming volumes."
findings.details: Confirmed by reading sources/2026-08/podman-61-adds-volume-rename-machine-restart-and-a-quadlet-imagevolume-key/source-0.html.gz (GitHub release notes, no match) and source-1.html.gz (Linuxiac, exact match) directly.

content_preview.summary: Podman 6.1 ships volume renaming, a machine restart command, Quadlet ImageVolume support, and IPv6 rootless port forwarding.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Podman 6.1 shipped on August 12, 2026, adding commands to rename volumes and restart Podman-managed virtual machines, alongside updates to Quadlet, networking, Kubernetes integration, and Docker API compatibility, according to the [release notes](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/releases/tag/v6.1.0) published on GitHub. editor_notes.content_quality: Dense, accurate feature-list Briefing appropriate for a release-notes roundup. Correctly distinguishes 'What We Know' facts from an 'Analysis' section framed as interpretation.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both snapshots directly. Every other feature/bugfix claim in the article (machine restart, --ignore/--retry flags, Quadlet ImageVolume=, generate kube livenessProbe, force_port_listen, IPv6 Pesto forwarding, free-memory reporting, the SSH-hang bugfix, the volume prune label-filter bugfix, the corrupt-systemd-units race condition, the /dev/kmsg-to-stderr change, and all four dependency version bumps) traces verbatim to the GitHub release notes. Only the 'without recreating them' quote fragment does not -- it's Linuxiac's paraphrase, misattributed to the release notes link.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All substantive facts are accurate; the underlying claim (volumes can be renamed instead of recreated) is true and supported by both sources. The issue is attribution of a specific quoted phrase, not a fabricated fact.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate -- no prior Podman-specific archive coverage.
concerns: One quoted phrase ('without recreating them') is attributed to the release notes but actually originates from Linuxiac's paraphrase -- see the filed corrections record.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Approve with corrections. The article is accurate and well-sourced; the single misattribution is minor, isolated to a subordinate claim, and is honestly covered by a public corrections note.
